sentences.text: Sigaspis was an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Early Devonian period.
The type species Sigaspis lepidophora was described by Daniel Goujet in 1973.
Fossils of this fish were found on the island of Spitsbergen in Svalbard, Norway.
Sigaspis is considered one of the most basal members of the order Arthrodira.
It belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
The genus is classified within the class Placodermi.
Sigaspis lived between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago, spanning the Pragian to Emsian stages.
